preamble: A header isn't text you type at the top of the page — the top of the page isn't somewhere you can put your cursor. A header is a separate layer that Docs repeats on every page for you. So you can't write your way into one; you have to ask Docs to create the layer first, and then it lets you type there.
generalization: Anything that belongs to the page rather than to the text — headers, footers, page numbers, breaks — lives together under Insert, in the group about page elements. When something won't accept your cursor, that's the signal: it isn't part of the document body, and you add it rather than type it.

steps.intent: You're not changing how existing text looks — you're bringing something into the document that isn't there yet. That's the difference between Format and Insert, and it's the question worth asking before you open any menu.
hints: Nothing in the document needs reformatting. Something new needs to exist.
The Insert menu, in the menu bar near the top left.

wrongHints.Format: Format changes text that already exists. There's no header yet to format — it has to be created first.
wrongHints.View: View changes how the document is displayed to you. A header is part of the document itself, and will print.

steps.intent: The header isn't at the top level of this menu, because Docs separates things that fill a page from things that structure one. A header belongs to the page frame, alongside footers, page numbers and breaks — look for the group that gathers them.
hints: A header isn't content you're dropping in at the cursor. It belongs to the page itself.
'Page elements', partway down the Insert menu, with an arrow showing a submenu.

wrongHints.Table: A table is content that sits in the flow of the document. A header sits outside that flow, on every page.
wrongHints.Break: Close in spirit — breaks are page furniture too — but a break divides the body text rather than adding a repeating band above it.

steps.intent: Your turn, with no highlight. The submenu holds a matched pair: one band above the text and one below. Pick the one that sits at the top, and Docs will create the layer and drop your cursor straight into it.
hints: Two options here are mirror images of each other. You want the one at the top of the page.
In the submenu that just opened, above the entry for its counterpart at the bottom of the page.

wrongHints.Footer: Same idea, opposite end — a footer repeats at the bottom of every page. Header is the one above the text.
wrongHints.Page numbers: Page numbers live inside a header or footer, but choosing them commits you to a particular content. Header gives you the empty band to write whatever you want.
